grammar_focus: 强调句 It is … that/who …、虚拟语气(与过去相反)+ 省略 if 的倒装(had not … been …)、现在分词短语修饰名词(a waterspout shooting down)、插入语(as it has come to be known / they found)、情态完成式 might/must/could have done(对过去的推测)(原创承载 NCE3 第三册 L42 考点·无需净化:洞穴探险科普——描写世界最深洞之一 Gouffre Berger 的下探·探险说明文;第三册无 KS 页,考点由课文结构自取;美式化 caving/colors)
scene: 洞穴勘查——或者说如今人们所熟知的“洞穴探险”——是一项比较新的运动。也许正是对独处的渴望,或是意外发现的机会,把人引向地下深处。要对一个洞穴探险者的动机作出令人满意的解释,是不可能的。对他来说,洞穴的那种奇特魅力,就像高山对登山者的魅力一样;它们唤起某种只能隐约体会的本能。探测真正深的洞穴,可不是星期天下午散步的人能胜任的。这类行动需要军事行动般的周密筹划和远见。有时得花整整八天来搭好绳梯、建立补给点,然后才能下到一个很深的洞里。这样的防范是必要的,因为无法预料洞穴探险者究竟会遇上什么样的困难。世界上已知最深的洞穴之一,是格勒诺布尔附近的高弗·伯杰洞,深达三千七百多英尺。这道巨大的陷坑,是一条地下暗流冲穿岩石的一道裂缝、慢慢冲蚀而成的。洞口高踞阿尔卑斯山的一处高原之上,宽仅约六英尺,很难被人察觉。要不是一位著名的法国洞穴探险家伯杰偶然发现了洞口,这个洞也许永远无人知晓。前不久,一支探险队下到了高弗·伯杰洞。钻过狭窄的洞口后,他们沿陡峭的洞壁往下爬,直到来到一条狭窄的通道。他们只能侧身沿通道慢慢挪动,有时蹚过浅溪,有时游过深潭。忽然,他们来到一道瀑布前,瀑布跌入洞底的一个地下湖。他们把装备装上一只充气橡皮艇,让水流载着他们渡到对岸,还穿上特制的橡胶服,以防冰冷的湖水。在远端,他们能听见一阵不断的轰鸣声,他们发现,那是一股从洞顶冲下的小水柱造成的。从岩石的一道裂隙中挤过去,探险者们来到一个巨大的洞穴,大得像座音乐厅。打开强光灯,他们看见一根根石笋——有的高达四十多英尺——像树干般拔地而起,去迎接从洞顶垂下的钟乳石。四周,一堆堆石灰石在彩虹般的各色光芒中闪烁。在洞穴那诡异的寂静里,唯一的声响,是从头顶高高的穹顶上不断滴落的水滴。

grammar_card.title: 强调句 It is…that / 虚拟倒装 had not…been / 分词修饰名词 / 插入语 / might have done
grammar_card.intro: ①强调句 It is/was + 被强调部分 + that/who + 其余:It is the desire … that lures people down。②与过去事实相反的虚拟语气,若省略 if,要把 had 提到句首倒装:had not the entrance been spotted=if the entrance had not been spotted。③现在分词短语可放在名词后修饰它:a waterspout shooting down。④插入语补充说明,不影响主句:as it has come to be known;they found。⑤情态完成式 might/must/could have done,对过去作推测:might never have been discovered。

rows: It is the desire that lures
省略 if 的虚拟倒装
had not the entrance been spotted
分词修饰名词 / 插入语

specialRules.rule: 与过去相反的虚拟条件,省略 if 时把 had 提到主语前倒装:Had not the entrance been spotted, …(=If the entrance had not been spotted, …)。
情态动词 + have + 过去分词表示对过去的推测:might have(也许)、must have(一定)、could have(本可以却没)。
美式:caving(英式 pot-holing)、color(英式 colour)、flashlight(英式 torch)。本课已按美语写。

prelisten.q: Listen and answer — With what does the writer compare the Gouffre Berger?

passage: Cave exploration, or caving, as it has come to be known, is a relatively new sport. Perhaps it is the desire for solitude, or the chance of making an unexpected discovery, that lures people down into the depths of the earth. It is impossible to give a satisfactory explanation for a caver's motives. For him, caves hold the same peculiar fascination that high mountains hold for the climber; they arouse instincts that can only be dimly understood. Exploring really deep caves is not a task for the Sunday afternoon rambler. Such undertakings require the precise planning and foresight of a military operation. It can take as long as eight days to rig up rope ladders and set up supply bases before a descent can be made into a very deep cave. Precautions of this sort are necessary, for it is impossible to foretell the exact nature of the difficulties that will confront the caver. One of the deepest known caves in the world is the Gouffre Berger, near Grenoble, which reaches a depth of more than 3,700 feet. This immense chasm was formed by an underground stream that tunneled a course through a flaw in the rock. The entrance, high on a plateau in the Alps, is only about six feet across, so it is barely noticeable. The cave might never have been discovered had not the entrance been spotted by a distinguished French caver named Berger. A team of cavers recently went down the Gouffre Berger. After entering the narrow gap, they climbed down the steep sides until they reached a narrow corridor. They had to edge their way along it, sometimes wading across shallow streams or swimming across deep pools. Suddenly they came to a waterfall that dropped into an underground lake. They loaded their gear onto an inflatable rubber dinghy and let the current carry them across, wearing special rubber suits to protect themselves from the icy water. At the far end they could hear an insistent booming sound, which they found was caused by a small waterspout shooting down from the roof. Squeezing through a cleft in the rock, the cavers arrived at an enormous cavern, as large as a concert hall. When they switched on their powerful lights, they saw great stalagmites — some of them over forty feet high — rising up like tree trunks to meet the stalactites hanging from the roof. All around, piles of limestone glistened in every color of the rainbow. In the eerie silence of the cavern, the only sound was water dripping from the high dome above them.

grammar_points.name: 虚拟语气 + 省略 if 的倒装(had not … been)
现在分词短语修饰名词(a waterspout shooting down)
插入语(as it has come to be known)
情态完成式 might/must/could have done

stage5.stem: "It is the desire for solitude ___ lures people underground."(强调句 It is … ___ …)
stage5.stem_cn: 正是对独处的渴望,把人引向地下。

stage5.stem: "It was in the Alps ___ the deepest cave was found."(强调地点,It was … ___ …)
stage5.stem_cn: 正是在阿尔卑斯山,人们发现了最深的洞。

stage5.stem: "It is the cavers ___ explore the deepest caves."(强调人,It is … ___ …)
stage5.stem_cn: 正是洞穴探险者们探索着最深的洞。

stage5.stem: "The cave might never have been discovered ___ not the entrance been spotted."(省略 if 的虚拟倒装,填助动词)
stage5.stem_cn: 要不是有人发现了洞口,这个洞也许永远无人知晓。

stage5.stem: "___ they planned more carefully, they would have gone deeper."(省略 if 的虚拟倒装:如果他们…)
stage5.stem_cn: 若是计划得更周密,他们本可以下得更深。

stage5.stem: "If the stream had not tunneled the rock, the chasm ___ never have formed."(与过去事实相反,主句用 ___ have done)
stage5.stem_cn: 要不是溪水冲蚀岩石,这陷坑根本不会形成。

stage5.stem: "They heard a waterspout ___ down from the roof."(现在分词短语修饰 waterspout)
stage5.stem_cn: 他们听见一股水柱从洞顶冲下。

stage5.stem: "Great stalagmites, ___ up like tree trunks, filled the cavern."(现在分词短语修饰 stalagmites)
stage5.stem_cn: 一根根石笋像树干般拔地而起,布满大洞。

stage5.stem: "They saw stalactites ___ from the roof."(分词修饰 stalactites:悬挂着的)
stage5.stem_cn: 他们看见钟乳石从洞顶垂下。

stage5.stem: "Cave exploration, ___ it has come to be known, is a new sport."(插入语"正如已被人熟知的那样")
stage5.stem_cn: 洞穴勘查——正如现在人们所熟知的——是项新运动。

stage5.stem: "The Gouffre Berger, ___ is near Grenoble, is very deep."(补充说明的从句,用哪个)
stage5.stem_cn: 高弗·伯杰洞——它在格勒诺布尔附近——非常深。

stage5.stem: "The sound, ___ they found, came from a waterspout."(插入语"他们发现",用哪个)
stage5.stem_cn: 那声音——他们发现——来自一股水柱。

stage5.stem: "The cave ___ never have been found without Berger."(对过去的推测"也许永远不会…")
stage5.stem_cn: 没有伯杰,这个洞也许永远不会被发现。

stage5.stem: "They were exhausted; they ___ have walked for hours."(有把握地推测过去"一定走了")
stage5.stem_cn: 他们精疲力竭,一定走了好几个小时。

stage5.stem: "It's a pity they didn't go further; they ___ have reached the bottom."("本可以…却没有")
stage5.stem_cn: 可惜他们没再往前,本可以到达洞底。

stage5.stem: "To tempt or attract someone into doing something is to ___ them."("引诱、吸引"用哪个词)
stage5.stem_cn: 引诱、吸引某人去做某事。

stage5.stem: "The ability to plan wisely for the future is ___."("预见、深谋远虑"用哪个词)
stage5.stem_cn: 对未来明智筹划的能力。

stage5.stem: "A strange, frightening quietness in a dark place feels ___."("引起恐惧的、可怕的"用哪个词)
stage5.stem_cn: 黑暗处那种诡异、令人发怵的寂静。
